blocking_findings.finding: Task .3 simultaneously requires PdfPageView to import TextLayer from pdfjs-dist and requires that no module outside lib/pdf.ts import pdfjs-dist. Both acceptance conditions cannot be satisfied.
blocking_findings.required_change: Make lib/pdf.ts export every required PDF.js runtime/type surface, including TextLayer and exception classifiers, and require PdfPageView/hooks to import only from that facade; alternatively narrow the single-import rule explicitly, but keep one coherent enforceable contract.

blocking_findings.finding: The task order is not executable as written. Task .1 must test real worker/cMap/font routes from pdfjs-dist, while task .2 adds the dependency. The instruction to install it locally or coordinate would create an untracked dependency state and defeats task isolation and reproducibility.
blocking_findings.required_change: Record the clean baseline first, then execute dependency/bootstrap task .2 before the route implementation in .1, or split dependency pinning into the first task. Add explicit dependency edges/order to the task artifacts.

blocking_findings.finding: R3 requires an actual non-embedded-font/CJK fixture to prove local cMap and standard-font loading offline, but task .2 does not create one and task .6 only names link, corrupt, JavaScript-action, password, and generated large fixtures. Checking that asset routes return 200 does not prove PDF.js requests and uses them during rendering.
blocking_findings.required_change: Add a deterministic small PDF fixture that genuinely requires a served cMap and/or non-embedded standard font. Require browser assertions that it renders correctly, that the expected local asset requests occur successfully, and that no non-self request occurs.

blocking_findings.finding: The browser-evidence task does not fully cover mandatory evidence. It lacks explicit aligned-selection screenshots at 100%, fit-width, and 200%; does not define a way to exercise loading, progressive, zero-page, and worker/cMap/font bootstrap-failure states in the running app; and does not explicitly verify the mobile overview card and rails on PDF documents.
blocking_findings.required_change: Specify fixtures or deterministic route-delay/failure controls for every R8 state, capture the three R6 alignment screenshots, and add browser assertions/screenshots for overview-card and rail behavior at required widths and themes.

blocking_findings.finding: Performance acceptance is not objectively implementable. P-3 has no numeric render-task bound; P-4 calls for p95 but the plan provides no repetition/sample protocol; and P-6 proposes reading a component counter after navigation even though the component and its state will have unmounted. The instrumentation ownership and production exposure mechanism are also unspecified.
blocking_findings.required_change: Define a numeric P-3 threshold tied to the 200-page fixture and scroll procedure, define P-4 sample count and p95 calculation, and specify a test-only global or event-based instrumentation channel that survives unmount and records render starts, cancels, settles, cleanup ordering, document destruction, and post-navigation activity.

blocking_findings.finding: The React StrictMode lifecycle contract is contradictory. The task requires loadingTask creation inside the effect, destruction during cleanup, and also a test asserting no duplicate load under StrictMode. React StrictMode intentionally re-runs effects in development, so two loading tasks may be created unless an additional cache/deduplication design is specified.
blocking_findings.required_change: State the intended invariant precisely: either allow StrictMode's first task to be created and promptly destroyed while forbidding concurrent surviving tasks/stale writes, or specify and test a concrete deduplication mechanism. Include URL-change and retry race tests with out-of-order promise resolution.

blocking_findings.finding: The fallback contract is incomplete. PdfViewer's callback only sets showRawView=true, but no state or prop is defined to carry the required explanatory fallback notice into DocView's Text branch. Automatic fallback behavior is therefore ambiguous and cannot satisfy R9 reliably.
blocking_findings.required_change: Define explicit fallback state and data flow, such as an onFallback(reason) callback or notice state owned by DocView. Require tests that corrupt, password, network, and bootstrap failures switch to Text when available while displaying the correct persistent notice, and remain actionable when extracted text is unavailable.

blocking_findings.finding: The docs task only records the canonical hosted gno.sh update as a follow-up, but repository instructions require hosted website documentation to be updated in the same change when user-facing behavior, API output, troubleshooting, or product claims change. The listed five local documentation surfaces are therefore insufficient for completion.
blocking_findings.required_change: Add the relevant files in /home/claw/work/gno.sh to the plan and require its check, typecheck, build, locally driven browser QA, and evidence. If deployment is outside this spec, distinguish pre-merge site updates and local QA from post-merge deployment rather than deferring the documentation itself.

non_blocking_observations.observation: Range coverage is otherwise strong: closed, open-ended, suffix, malformed, unsatisfiable, multi-range, image regression, Content-Range, Content-Length, Accept-Ranges, and Content-Disposition are named. Add HEAD behavior tests for the new vendor routes because the spec promises GET/HEAD.

Realpath hardening must canonicalize both the configured root and the existing candidate before containment comparison. The planned ENOENT lexical fallback should remain limited to genuinely missing candidates; permission and other realpath errors must fail closed.

The plan correctly preserves strict CSP, frame-ancestors 'none', object-src 'none', and X-Frame-Options DENY. It should also assert the no-unsafe-eval condition directly rather than relying only on the JavaScript-action browser fixture.

Keyboard and toolbar coverage is well scoped, but native PageUp/PageDown and arrow scrolling must call preventDefault only when the viewer actually handles the shortcut; otherwise keyboard users may get double movement.

Using basename(doc.relPath) as the relative asset path should be validated against recordSourcePath/container-backed document cases. A test should prove the derived URL resolves the actual indexed PDF and cannot select a sibling with a coincident filename.

The package-smoke extension is appropriately aimed at a packed global install, but it should launch the installed binary rather than repository source and verify response bodies match files from the installed pdfjs-dist dependency, not merely status and size.

UI implementation is subject to the mandatory frontend-design plugin instruction. The execution plan should confirm that capability is available before tasks .3-.5 begin or document the blocking escalation path.

coverage_summary: All R1-R19 are nominally mapped across the seven tasks, and the plan preserves the central security posture: same-origin assets, strict framing denial, no object/embed/iframe, HTTP(S)-only annotations, no scripting layer, Range containment hardening, bounded rendering, extracted-text deep links, package smoke, and final gates. However, nominal mapping is not sufficient: the current artifacts contain an impossible import rule, an invalid dependency order, no real cMap/non-embedded-font rendering fixture, incomplete browser-state and text-alignment evidence, undefined performance measurements, contradictory StrictMode acceptance, incomplete fallback-notice data flow, and deferred mandatory hosted documentation. Grok 4.5 should not begin implementation until these ambiguities are corrected.
